questions.prompt: Which part of a PLC runs the program?
options: The processor (CPU)
The power supply
The input module
The rack
questions.explanation: The processor reads the inputs, runs the program and writes the outputs. The modules connect it to the machine; the rack holds them.

questions.prompt: A small machine needs 8 inputs and 6 outputs, and will never grow. Which kind of PLC fits best?
options: A compact PLC: power supply, processor, inputs and outputs in one box
A modular PLC with a large rack
Two PLCs, one for inputs and one for outputs
No PLC: only relays can do this
questions.explanation: A compact (fixed) PLC is small and cheap, and has enough points for a small machine. A modular PLC suits larger machines that need more or different modules.

questions.prompt: A photo eye has an **NPN** (sinking) output: it connects the input to 0 V when it sees a part. Which kind of DC input does it need?
options: A sourcing input, which supplies the current
A sinking input, which also connects to 0 V
A triac output
A 120 V AC input
questions.explanation: One side sources, the other sinks. A sinking sensor needs a sourcing input to supply the current it takes to 0 V.

questions.prompt: Which of these field devices are wired to an **output** module? Choose every one.
options: A pilot light
A solenoid valve
A motor contactor's coil
A limit switch
A float switch
questions.explanation: Outputs drive things the PLC controls. Limit switches and float switches tell the PLC something, so they are inputs.

questions.prompt: This overheat alarm runs the working program, but one input has a wiring fault. Turn the Thermostat to Too hot, press **Alarm reset** on the machine, and watch the alarm and the rungs. Which fault does it have?
options: The thermostat's wire is broken: Overheat always reads FALSE
The thermostat is shorted: Overheat always reads TRUE
The Alarm reset button is shorted: ResetPB always reads TRUE
The Alarm reset button's wire is broken: ResetPB always reads FALSE
questions.explanation: The alarm never comes on, however hot it gets: on the rungs, Overheat stays FALSE in Too hot. A broken wire reads the same as "all is well", so this switch fails unsafe. That is why sensors that guard against danger are wired so that a broken wire looks like the danger (normally closed), as the Stop button is.

questions.prompt: This press guard runs the working program, but one input has a wiring fault. Leave the Guard switch at Open, then press both hand buttons, and watch the lights and the rungs. Which fault does it have?
options: The guard switch is shorted: GuardShut always reads TRUE, even with the guard open
The guard switch's wire is broken: GuardShut always reads FALSE
The Left hand button is shorted: LeftHand always reads TRUE
The Right hand button's wire is broken: RightHand always reads FALSE
questions.explanation: With the guard open, Ready is lit, Guard open is dark, and both hands close the press: on the rungs GuardShut reads TRUE whatever the switch does. A broken guard-switch wire would keep the press from ever closing, and a faulty hand button would change what the hands do, not the guard lights.

questions.prompt: A PLC's scan time is 5 ms. How many times does it read its inputs in one second?
questions.explanation: The inputs are read once per scan: 1000 ms / 5 ms = 200 scans a second.

questions.prompt: A program has a coil of Pump on rung 2 and another coil of Pump on rung 9. Rung 2 passes power; rung 9 does not. What is written to the Pump output at the end of the scan?
options: FALSE: rung 9 runs later and overwrites rung 2
TRUE: rung 2 turned it on first
TRUE for half the scan, then FALSE
Nothing: the PLC refuses to run the program
questions.explanation: Rungs run top to bottom, and the last coil of a tag wins. This double coil mistake is fixed by putting both conditions in parallel on one rung.

questions.prompt: Write the IEC address of **input** byte 0, bit 2.
questions.explanation: %I is an input, X a single bit, then byte 0, bit 2. An output would be %QX0.2.

questions.prompt: Match each Allen-Bradley address to what it is.

pairs.right: SLC or MicroLogix: input, slot 1, bit 0
SLC or MicroLogix: output, slot 2, bit 3
SLC or MicroLogix: a memory bit, file B3, word 0, bit 1
Logix: the input module in slot 1, bit 0

questions.explanation: The older SLC and MicroLogix PLCs use file letters (I, O, B); Logix controllers name the module's slot and its data. Either way, a good program gives the point a readable tag name.
